title: Considerations for Classifying "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship" as Objectionable under Undesirable Publications Act
what_it_is: Considerations for Classifying "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship" as Objectionable under Undesirable Publications Act

sections.label: Red Lines book classification question
sections.summary: MP asked about considerations and significance of IMDA classifying "Red Lines" as objectionable under the Undesirable Publications Act for the Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs what are the considerations and significance of IMDA classifying the book "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship” as objectionable under the Undesirable Publications Act (UPA) to the Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It contained material that denigrated several religions and religious figures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: These included caricatures from the Charlie Hebdo magazine of the Prophet Muhammad, which demean the Prophet and are extremely offensive to Muslims.

sections.label: MUIS review of Red Lines
sections.summary: MUIS reviewed the "Red Lines" book and found caricatures of the Prophet, content inciting discrimination against Muslims, mocking the Holy Quran and Prophet, and demeaning Islam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: MUIS reviewed the "Red Lines" book and found it contained several caricatures of the Prophet, as well as others that incited discrimination against Muslims, mocked the Holy Quran and the Prophet, and demeaned Islam.

sections.label: Six other objectionable publications
sections.summary: IMDA had deemed six other publications objectionable in the last five years for denigrating various religious communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In my earlier reply, I have also said that IMDA had, in the last five years, deemed six other publications to be objectionable, for denigrating various religious communities.

sections.label: IMDA and prohibited online content
sections.summary: IMDA expects adherence to standards and may deem websites glorifying ethnic, racial or religious hatred as prohibited material under the Broadcasting Act's Internet Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: IMDA certainly expects them to adhere to their very own standards strictly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But in addition, when IMDA is alerted to the existence of websites that glorify, insight or endorse ethnic, racial or religious hatred, strife or intolerance, it may deem such content as prohibited material under the Broadcasting Act's Internet Code of Practice.

sections.label: Facebook post blocked in Singapore
sections.summary: IMDA assessed a post as prohibited content breaching the Internet Code of Practice, requested Facebook remove it, and Facebook blocked it for Singapore users.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: IMDA assessed that the post contains prohibited content on the grounds of national harmony and is in the clear breach of the Internet Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: IMDA issued a request to Facebook to remove the post and Facebook subsequently blocked it from access by users in Singapore.

sections.label: IMDA seeks views on religious content
sections.summary: IMDA seeks views of relevant agencies before deciding on content affecting religious harmony, including content comparing religions or views within a religion.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: IMDA seeks the views of relevant agencies before making its decision on content that could affect religious harmony, and this is inclusive of content that may compare different religions or within the same religion, have different views.
